The buggy method is `org.joda.time.Partial.with(org.joda.time.DateTimeFieldType, int)`.

Static evidence:
- In [Partial.java](/abs/path/??) `with(...)` gets the added field’s duration at line 439 and only searches for an insertion point if `unitField.isSupported()` is true.

Because unsupported durations compare as equal and both `era` and `year` have no range duration here, it throws `Types array must not contain duplicate: era and year` even though they are distinct field types.

So the root cause is not the constructor; it is `Partial.with(...)` building the field array in the wrong order when the new field has an unsupported duration or no range. The fix should be in the insertion-order logic in `with(...)`, not in the duplicate check exception itself.
